summary: OpenAI began a limited preview of the GPT-5.6 model family (Sol, Terra, Luna), a new flagship generation with stronger agentic coding, biology and cybersecurity capabilities, a new layered safety stack, updated pricing and caching terms, and a Cerebras-hosted deployment option.

mechanisms.reason: The document explicitly frames GPT-5.6 Sol as crossing a capability threshold requiring a phased, safeguarded release.
mechanisms.quote: That uncertainty, along with the model’s broader step change in capabilities, is why we are pairing the model’s increased capabilities with stronger safeguards and a phased release.

mechanisms.reason: Terra delivers comparable performance to GPT-5.5 at half the price and GeneBench results improve while using fewer tokens, both stating reduced work per unit of output.
mechanisms.quote: Terra has competitive performance to GPT‑5.5 while being 2x cheaper and Luna brings strong capability at our lowest cost.

mechanisms.reason: The new ultra mode explicitly moves beyond single-agent execution to coordinated subagents completing delegated work.
mechanisms.quote: we’re introducing a new `ultra` mode that goes beyond the capabilities of a single agent by leveraging subagents to accelerate complex work.

mechanisms.reason: New explicit cache breakpoints and a minimum 30-minute cache life describe a more persistent KV-cache architecture that increases memory footprint per served request.
mechanisms.quote: GPT‑5.6 also introduces more predictable prompt caching, including support for explicit cache breakpoints and a 30-minute minimum cache life.

mechanisms.reason: The U.S. government required a restricted, government-vetted preview before broader release, gating access to the model on national-security grounds tied to its cyber capabilities.
mechanisms.quote: At their request, we are starting with a limited preview for a small group of trusted partners whose participation has been shared with the government, before releasing more broadly.

mechanisms.reason: A new maximum reasoning effort mode gives the model more time (and thus more compute/tokens) to reason per query, increasing aggregate inference work.
mechanisms.quote: we’re introducing a new `max` reasoning effort to give Sol the most time to reason deeply.

categories.reason: OpenAI is deploying its flagship model on Cerebras silicon for high-speed inference, directing demand to a non-GPU accelerator vendor.
categories.quote: We're also launching GPT‑5.6 Sol on Cerebras at up to 750 tokens per second in July, bringing frontier intelligence to customers at unprecedented speed.

practices.reason: New state-of-the-art coding and long-horizon agentic/cyber results are lab-reported and preview-only, warranting independent verification before depending on them.
practices.quote: we share a set of evaluations highlighting improved agentic capabilities in coding, biology, and cybersecurity

practices.reason: Named benchmarks (Terminal-Bench 2.1, GeneBench v1, ExploitBench, ExploitGym) and a Preparedness Framework threshold give a measurement bar to check our own systems against, though results are the lab's own.
practices.quote: On ExploitBench ², GPT‑5.6 Sol is competitive with Mythos Preview using only ~1/3 of the output tokens.

practices.reason: Cache billing terms change (writes at 1.25x uncached rate) and require adjusting caching strategy and cost estimates for any team integrating the API.
practices.quote: For GPT‑5.6 and later models, cache writes are billed at 1.25x the model’s uncached input rate, while cache reads continue to receive the 90% cached-input discount.

practices.reason: A subagent-based ultra mode is mentioned but without a stated gain or implementation detail to build against yet.
practices.quote: we’re introducing a new `ultra` mode that goes beyond the capabilities of a single agent by leveraging subagents to accelerate complex work.

practices.reason: The Cerebras deployment shows a speed gain but it is tied to third-party infrastructure not under our control.
practices.quote: We're also launching GPT‑5.6 Sol on Cerebras at up to 750 tokens per second in July

notable_reason: A frontier model family release gated behind a U.S. government-mandated limited preview due to cyber capability concerns is an unusual and consequential regulatory/capability event worth surfacing.
